item.title: A lump. A pregnancy. A breast cancer diagnosis: How one Staten Island mom fought for both lives
item.dc:creator: Dr. Gracelyn Santos
item.description: There are 143.9 breast cases per 100,000 people annually — 11.5% higher than New York City’s rate of 129.1 and 4.8% higher than New York state’s rate of 137.3.
item.content:encoded:
EDITOR’S NOTE: Staten Island has some of the highest cancer rates in New York—and for many families, the question isn’t just about diagnosis, but why. In this series, “Cancer on Staten Island: The Search for Why,” the Advance/SILive.com will examine what data, public health studies and environmental research reveal about cancer in the borough, while also elevating the voices of the people living it.

STATEN ISLAND, N.Y. — For Deana Jean, March 24, 2016, was a date that changed her life forever.

media:content.media:description: Deana Jean is a Staten Islander and breast cancer survivor. (Advance/SILive.com | Scott Axelrod)

item.title: Staten Island artist dreamed up a ferry-eating octopus. Now he’s putting mobsters in ‘cement shoes’
item.dc:creator: Jack Bulik
item.description: The Staten Island artist behind the infamous Ferry-eating giant octopus is back with another wild New York tale. This time, Joe Reginella is bringing the mob legend of “cement shoes” to life.
item.content:encoded: STATEN ISLAND, N.Y. – Joe Reginella has a “King Kong” poster hanging on the wall of his Staten Island studio, a fitting backdrop for an artist who has spent years turning monsters, disasters and wildly improbable tales into New York City “history.”

media:content.media:description: Joe Reginella stands with his recent fictional memorial.
